quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should you do when you approach a traffic light that is not working?

options.text: Stop completely and let others go first before entering the intersection.
You do not need to stop if the intersection is empty.
Drive fast through the intersection to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and let others go first before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection as an all-way stop. Always come to a complete stop. Look around and let other vehicles go first before you enter the intersection.

questions.question: When should your wheels NOT point straight ahead?

options.text: When you are waiting to turn left at a traffic light.
When you are parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
When you are parked on a flat road with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
questions.explanation: When waiting to turn left, keep your wheels straight. This prevents you from sliding into oncoming traffic if someone hits you from behind. On a hill, turn your wheels so your car will not roll into traffic if your brakes fail.

questions.question: A broken yellow line in the middle of the road means:

options.text: You cannot pass other vehicles.
You can pass on the right when it is safe.
You can pass on the left when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass another vehicle on the left if no vehicles are coming toward you. Never cross a solid yellow line to pass.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should check your mirrors and:

options.text: Never look over your shoulder.
Always slow down in your current lane.
Look quickly over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look quickly over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check for vehicles you might not see in your mirrors. Make sure no other cars are moving into the same spot from another lane.

questions.question: This sign warns you about:

options.text: A steep hill ahead.
Trucks are not allowed on the upcoming hill.
A logging road is coming up.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you a steep hill is coming. Slow down and be ready to control your speed to protect your brakes.

questions.question: Roads are most slippery:

options.text: After it has been raining hard for many hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Right when rain starts to fall.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when rain starts to fall.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery in the first 30 minutes of rain. Water mixes with oil and dirt on the road that has not washed away yet. Drive carefully on slippery roads.

questions.question: You should leave extra space when following:

options.text: A station wagon.
A driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
A small car.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, and vehicles with trailers cannot see vehicles directly behind them. Stay farther back so they can see you. Large vehicles also block your view of the road ahead, so increase your distance to see around them.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires slide on water instead of the road. How do you prevent it in wet weather?

options.text: Use cruise control to maintain the same speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts raining.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is caused by driving too fast on wet roads. Slow down when the road is wet to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and use low beam headlights.
Slow down and use high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use your low beam headlights. If you cannot see ahead, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: One-way traffic only.
An intersection is ahead.
Traffic is merging from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is merging from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They warn you about conditions coming up. This sign tells you to be ready to let traffic safely merge from the right.

questions.question: Backing your vehicle is:

options.text: Always dangerous.
Dangerous if you have a helper.
Only dangerous in large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always dangerous.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see clearly behind your vehicle. Always use extra caution when backing up.

questions.question: When a car with bright headlights drives toward you at night, you should:

options.text: Stop until the other driver passes.
Look below their headlights.
Glance toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Glance toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at bright headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes. This prevents you from being blinded.

questions.question: A broken yellow line down the center of a road means:

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means any driver may pass when no oncoming traffic is present.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines down the center of a road mean that passing is:

options.text: Allowed from both directions.
Allowed only from your direction of travel.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no driver from either direction can cross it to pass.

questions.question: You are driving on a one-way street. You may turn left onto another one-way street only if:

options.text: You increase your speed before the turn.
Traffic on the street moves to the right.
Traffic on the street moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic on the street moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You may turn left onto a one-way street only if traffic moves to the left. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: Before entering a curve, you should:

options.text: Activate your turn signal.
Reduce your speed.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Slow down before a curve. Curves require lower speeds for safety. Braking hard in a curve may cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: When driving on the freeway behind a large truck, you should drive:

options.text: Closer behind the truck than you would a passenger vehicle.
Farther behind the truck than you would a passenger vehicle.
To the right side of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther behind the truck than you would a passenger vehicle.
questions.explanation: Follow farther behind a large truck because trucks have large blind spots where the driver cannot see.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a downhill ramp that curves. You should:

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.
Start braking after you enter the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before a curve. Braking in a curve may cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: The correct way to make a right turn is to:

options.text: Signal, slow down, and get into the lane closest to the centerline before turning.
Signal, slow down, and get into the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
Approach from the right lane, then move toward the middle of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and get into the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Signal your turn. Slow down. Move into the right lane and stay close to the right curb before turning.

questions.question: Any amount of alcohol in the blood can affect a driver's:

options.text: Right-of-way privileges.
Judgment and physical coordination.
Knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol can affect your judgment and coordination. Even small amounts of alcohol can impair your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, like school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.
Watch for multiple trains.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: You must be very careful at all railroad crossings. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Watch for vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, such as school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.

questions.question: Large trucks are likely to lose speed when:

options.text: Driving up long or steep hills.
Driving in long, gradual curves.
Driving down long, gradual hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving up long or steep hills.
questions.explanation: Large trucks take longer to speed up than smaller vehicles. They can lose speed when driving up long or steep hills. Leave extra space behind a large truck, especially on hills.

questions.question: When driving on a slippery surface, such as snow or ice:

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Maintain traction by following other vehicles closely.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: To avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, shift to a low gear before going down a steep hill. Stay farther back from the vehicle in front of you than you normally would. Avoid sudden stops. If you do not have antilock brakes, pump your brakes to slow down or stop.

questions.question: If a road is slippery, maintain a following distance that is:

options.text: No different than normal.
Farther from the car ahead than normal.
Closer to the car ahead than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther from the car ahead than normal.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle needs a longer distance to stop on a slippery road than on a dry road. Leave more space between you and the car ahead when driving on slippery roads.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must travel through the intersection at the posted speed limit.
The maximum speed limit under ideal conditions is 55 mph.
You must not travel below the speed indicated.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed limit under ideal conditions is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the maximum speed allowed on this road. You can drive slower if road conditions require it, but you cannot drive faster than the posted speed limit.
